Nel carcinoma dell'endometrio la RM serv:
In endometrial carcinoma, MRI is used to estimate three things before surgery: the depth of myometrial invasion (less or more than 50%), cervical stromal invasion and extension beyond the uterus (serosa, adnexa, parametria, vagina, lymph nodes).

The key sequences are high-resolution T2 oriented along the axis of the uterus, diffusion and dynamic T1 after gadolinium (equilibrium phase at about 2-3 minutes): the tumor has intermediate signal on T2, restricts diffusion and enhances less than the myometrium. An intact junctional zone and a continuous subendometrial enhancement band indicate absence of deep invasion.

Pitfalls: bulky polypoid masses distend the cavity and thin the myometrium, making measurement difficult (compare the thickness of tumor within the myometrium with the total thickness); leiomyomas and adenomyosis make the junctional zone less reliable; in postmenopausal women the junctional zone is often not visible. The definitive stage is surgical-pathological (FIGO 2009: IA <50%, IB ≥50%, II cervical stroma; FIGO 2023 adds histotype and molecular data).

In this case the residual myometrium is thin around a very bulky mass: the MRI picture is consistent with deep invasion, but the estimate is difficult; the collection histology reports pT1b (invasion ≥50%), N0.
